taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: a 8-step plan, read from the schema reply
2 verdicts, each read from the schema reply
1 revision, each called for by a verdict
5 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
The verifier was right. I replaced the 10 sentence fragments with complete sentences from each code's own section of RFC 9110. I checked every new quote against the text of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html in this session, using `find` and reading the page at the matching offsets, and wrote them with single spaces.

**Changed:**
- **203, 308, 405, 410, 414, 501:** The full sentence is "A NNN response is heuristically cacheable; i.e., unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls (see Section 4.2.2 of [CACHING])." A search for that sentence finds it in each of these codes' own sections.
- **206:** Section 15.3.7 has a slightly different version: "A 206 response is heuristically cacheable; i.e., unless otherwise indicated by explicit cache controls (see Section 4.2.2 of [CACHING])."
- **307, 413, 422:** I used the full first sentence of each code's definition.

**Unchanged:** The 303 and 421 quotes were already complete sentences. The reason phrases, section numbers, cacheability values and URL also stay the same, since the verifier confirmed them.

**Why these values (RFC 9110, still the current HTTP Semantics specification):** Section 15.1 lists 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414 and 501 as heuristically cacheable and says "all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable." So 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 are false. The current reason phrases for 413 and 422 are "Content Too Large" and "Unprocessable Content."

| Code | Reason | Section | Heuristically cacheable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 203 | Non-Authoritative Information | 15.3.4 | yes |
| 206 | Partial Content | 15.3.7 | yes |
| 303 | See Other | 15.4.4 | no |
| 307 | Temporary Redirect | 15.4.8 | no |
| 308 | Permanent Redirect | 15.4.9 | yes |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed | 15.5.6 | yes |
| 410 | Gone | 15.5.11 | yes |
| 413 | Content Too Large | 15.5.14 | no |
| 414 | URI Too Long | 15.5.15 | yes |
| 421 | Misdirected Request | 15.5.20 | no |
| 422 | Unprocessable Content | 15.5.21 | no |
| 501 | Not Implemented | 15.6.2 | yes |

Source for every row: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
